title: Hire Seeding Rotation Playbook — 14d Ambassador Program
content:
Summary:
This playbook describes a 14-day ‘Hire Seeding’ rotation that places new hires into short, focused ambassador assignments across 2–3 host teams. Purpose is to accelerate cross-team orientation, validate candidate-team fit quickly, and seed early contributor signals so hiring managers can make rapid, evidence-driven role decisions. This is intentionally lighter than a full 90-day plan — it’s a tactical experiment for batch hires and role discovery.

Objectives:
- Give each hire exposure to multiple product/infra areas within 14 days so both candidate and teams collect real signals.
- Surface early impact tasks that are reviewable within a week.
- Create a standardized checklist and feedback cadence so hiring managers can decide to convert, extend, or reassign candidates by day 14.
- Reduce onboarding overhead by centralizing coordination through an Ambassador role.

Scope and When to Use:
- Intended for small cohorts (2–8 hires) joining at similar times or for high-volume internship/grad intake.
- Not recommended for senior ICs who need deeper, role-specific ramp. Use only when hiring teams agree to trial rotation.

Roles & Responsibilities:
- People Ops (Program Lead — owner): coordinate schedule, logistics, assessment templates, and final conversion meeting.
- Ambassador (rotational engineer/PM/designer): 0.2 FTE per cohort; runs daily standups, keeps assignment board, triages low-friction tasks across host teams.
- Host Team Leads: provide 2–3 scoped tasks, a mentor (buddy), and quick review in the end-of-rotation demo.
- Candidate (new hire): complete 1 scoped task per host + demo + written reflection.

Success Metrics (first-pass):
- Decision rate by day 14 (convert / extend / reassign) >= 80% of cohort.
- Time-to-first-review median <= 9 days.
- Host team feedback average >= 3/5 on contribution and collaboration.

14-day schedule (high level):
- Day -2 to 0 (pre-start): access provisioned, cohort Slack channel created, Ambassador introduced; small prework: repo readme + environment smoke test.
- Day 0: welcome orientation (People Ops), team lightning intros, Ambassador-led kickoff, 30m with hiring manager.
- Day 1–3: Host Team A — pairing + scoped first task (3–6 hours). Daily 15m with Ambassador. End-of-host review (peer + mentor).
- Day 4–7: Host Team B — second task + integration test or doc update (3–6 hours). Mid-rotation sync with People Ops.
- Day 8–11: Host Team C (optional) or focused depth work for strongest matched area.
- Day 12: Demo prep and written reflection due.
- Day 13: Final demos (15m per candidate per host).
- Day 14: Decision meeting (Hiring manager + People Ops + Ambassador) -> convert / extend (30d) / reassign -> communicate decision and next steps.

Sample Scoped Task Patterns (low friction, high signal):
- Fix a failing unit test + write short regression test (engineering).
- Add a small dashboard metric and short README on interpretation (data/observability).
- Draft a short feature spec + acceptance criteria for a minor UI tweak (product/designer).
- Create or improve a quickstart in docs for an internal tool (developer experience).

Assessment Rubric (used by host mentors — single sheet, 1–5 scale):
- Technical correctness (1–5): did the deliverable meet requirements and standards?
- Learning velocity (1–5): how fast did candidate pick up unfamiliar context?
- Collaboration (1–5): communication, pair programming, receptiveness to feedback.
- Ownership & initiative (1–5): independently moved tasks forward, suggested improvements.
- Overall fit signal (1–5): would this candidate be a positive contributor on this host team?
Weights: Technical 30%, Learning 25%, Collaboration 20%, Ownership 15%, Fit 10%.
Decision rules:
- Convert: weighted score >= 3.6 and positive demo.
- Extend (30-day deep trial): weighted score 3.0–3.59 or mixed signals with manager wanting more evidence.
- Reassign/Decline: < 3.0 or clear mismatch.

Onboarding Checklists (Ambassador checklist — quick):
- Pre-arrival: accounts provisioned, environment steps sent, host assignment plan shared.
- Day 0: cohort welcome slides shared, Slack channel active, 1:1 calendar invites with hosts.
- Day 1–7: daily 15m standup, task card created in board, mentor tag assigned.
- Day 8–14: demo slots booked, reflection doc template submitted.

Communication Templates (short examples):
- Welcome Slack (sent by Ambassador): "Welcome @name! You’re seeded into Team A this week. Today meet @mentorA at 10:30 to pair on task #1. Ping me any infra issues. Short daily standup 4pm PT."
- Demo reminder: "Hi @host-team — candidate demo scheduled Thu 11:00. Please bring 15 min of feedback using the rubric sheet."

Conversion Meeting Agenda (day 14):
- Quick recap of tasks completed (Ambassador) — 5m.
- Host mentor feedback (2–3m per host).
- Candidate self-reflection (2m).
- Hiring manager recommendation (3m).
- Decision and next steps (5m).

Risks & Mitigations:
- Over-scheduling hosts: cap scoped tasks at 6 hrs each and guarantee mentor bandwidth.
- Candidate overwhelm: include quiet day buffer and one focused depth day.
- Poor evidence quality: require at least one coded/observable artifact per host.

Operational templates (links and quick references):
- Rubric sheet (GH template): GH: /onboarding/rubric-seed.csv
- Candidate reflection template (Confluence): /PeopleOps/Seed-Reflection-Template
- Ambassador playbook checklist: small checklist in GH snippets.

Open questions & next experiments:
- Should conversion thresholds vary by role seniority? (proposal: raise bar for senior hires).
- Pilot metrics collection via simple Google sheet vs central HRIS integration.
- Evaluate peer-nominated ambassadors vs rotational paid ambassador slot.

Next steps (for approvers):
- Agree on ambassador staffing model and commit host teams for next cohort.
- Finalize rubric CSV and import into the weekly hiring review spreadsheet.
- Pilot with next intern cohort (June 2025).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is an experimental, low-friction approach — intended to shorten decision cycles for batch hires while preserving manager signal. Suggestions for alternative signal capture (video demos, recorded pairing sessions) welcome.

Document history: initial draft 2025-02-10 by Priya Nair; updated 2025-03-02 after People Ops sync.
